prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: .  Why do you change my assigned seats? You moved me 2 rows back on 1 flight & a row back on the other. Not full flights, plenty of other seats, many together.  I've now screenshot my seats. Unless there's an upgrade available, I'd appreciate them staying the same. Thanks!
Delta: Hi there. Sorry to hear that your seats were moved. Please share your confirmation number via DM so we can look into this.  *ALA

Customer: you didn’t let me choose a seat at a base fair, stuck me in the back row with no window and no recline and no choice. HORRIBLE. #delta #deltafail #worstairline #flyjetblue
Delta: ...you wish me to review your booking. *ADB 2/2

Customer: It’s (still) taking 25+ plus minutes to get from scanning my boarding pass to my seat  & takeoff is in 4 minutes.
Delta: Oh no! Let us know if we can assist.  *ALA

Customer: should I be worried if I'm not able to choose a seat for tomorrow's flight because "one of more passengers are on the standby list"? Does that mean I'm on that list too?
Delta: You are all set. I have assigned you an aisle seat. *TKR

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: service_complaint):
"""How come I can't choose my seat & have to get assigned at the gate when there are available seats on the map? (  )"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: We’re sorry for the inconvenience. Please DM us your confirmation number so we can review your reservation and help with seat selection.
